still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the permanent obesity benefit, and Medicare still reaches users only through diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban of its kind, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. One-line reconciliation: 45.0% ever − 35.4% current = 9.6% of adults used and are off now (3.0 cycled-and-off-again + 6.6 stopped once, incl. ~1.5 who joined since 2034 and already quit); restarters on drug now 15.0 pts (~42% of current users), so (15.0 + 3.0)/45.0 = 40% of ever-users have cycled. This fits one-year persistence near one-third on full-dose cash regimens, ~55% on low-dose plans, and higher (~60%) in conditional employer tracks where coverage depends on verified adherence; restart within a year still 36–47%. Age check: 0.20×23 + 0.33×36.5 + 0.24×47 + 0.23×32.5 = 4.6 + 12.05 + 11.28 + 7.48 ≈ 35.4. Income thirds average 35.3. 35.4% of ~276M adults ≈ 97.7M users, up ~21M. FICTIONAL adult payer mix: commercial ~20.5M (21%; ~13.0M of them in conditional 'earned coverage' or monitored tracks), Medicare ~15.5M (16%), Medicaid ~3.9M (4%), legitimate cash ~35.3M (36%), compounded under the 2035 retatrutide shortage listing ~4.2M (4%), imported/counterfeit/research-peptide ~18.3M (19%). Sum 97.7M. Cash breakdown: ~15.5M cash weight, ~11.0M longevity/'metabolic health', ~5.2M calm/focus, ~2.1M Reset, ~1.5M AUD. ~22M users have BMI under 30, ~7.5M under 25. Adult obesity ~30.9%. ~16% of adults have obesity and have never used, concentrated in the bottom third, the rural South and 65+ adults without qualifying codes. Off-drug: ~26.5M adults used and are off; ~22% of conditional-track enrollees failed a 6-month checkpoint in 2035–36 and lost coverage, about half of them moving to gray product. Pediatric: ~0.88M of ~73M under-18s on drug (1.2%); 12–17s ~3.0%; 6–11s ~0.4% nationally (≈0.6% in the 39 non-ban states holding ~69% of children, ~0% for weight indication in the eleven ban states). ~58% of children live in a household with a current user; ~6.8M live with a parent who regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Medicare reaches ~15.5M users only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk codes, all behind prior authorisation. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 15.5M × ~$225 average net/month × 12 ≈ $41.9B gross Part D incretin spend before rebate true-up, up from ~$36.5B; average net stayed at $225 because prices stalled. Dementia-risk route ~2.9M × ~$235 × 12 ≈ $8.2B, growing after the 2035 confirmatory readout. Medicaid ~3.9M adults, mostly diabetes codes; the same 7 states cover weight use and the same two condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress. Children: ~0.4M of the ~0.88M pediatric users are Medicaid/CHIP, reached in non-ban states through EPSDT medical-necessity review even where adult weight drugs are excluded.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide $3–25 a month across 150+ brands; Canadian generic CAD 45–80, Brazilian BRL 160–280. Chinese 'reta' vials $25–70, now joined by 'ami' (amycretin-sequence) and 'cagri' vials at $40–90. India's B2C export registration took effect Jan 2035 and cut direct India-to-US parcels by roughly a third; volume rerouted through UAE free zones, Mexico and the Dominican Republic. India and China still supply ~70% of world incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices stalled: no list or cash cut by any manufacturer in 2035–36. TrumpRx holds $149 starting oral, $179 Wegovy pill maintenance, $149–199 Foundayo, $229–279 injectable Wegovy/Zepbound. Retatrutide stays $299 all doses; MariTide $219 direct; amycretin $1,249 list; bimagrumab $1,150. Causes: EPI bellwether verdict and litigation reserves, a 2035 district ruling upholding Novo's semaglutide formulation patents against Paragraph IV filers, and retatrutide 12 mg demand outrunning fill capacity (FDA shortage list Apr 2035). Coverage became conditional rather than broader: employer weight coverage rose from 29% to 37% (Business Group on Health, Nov 2035), but ~31 of those 37 points are 'earned coverage' designs: six months covered, then continuation only with ≥90% verified adherence and ≥5% weight loss or HbA1c target, often paired with the 30% premium differential. Conditional and monitored tracks hold ~13.0M, inside the ~20.5M commercial users; ~7.0M take clinic-administered MariTide, total MariTide ~8.6M. Compounded retatrutide from 503A/503B pharmacies sells $129–199 via telehealth during the shortage (~4.2M). Imported/research-peptide channels ~18.3M, incl. ~6M on reta/ami vials. Orals ~48% of users. LSA reimbursement of calm/Reset platform fees rose from ~19% to ~24% of large employers.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new class reached market (next_gen_launch: none). The pediatric under-12 driver is realised through an existing product in a new population: Novo filed weekly semaglutide for ages 6–11 on STEP Young data in Dec 2034, and the FDA approved it in Dec 2035, 12 months later, with the liraglutide-style growth-velocity monitoring box and specialist-initiation recommendation. Tirzepatide's dementia confirmatory trial read out Jun 2035 (all-cause dementia HR ~0.86 in obesity plus CVD), converted to traditional approval Mar 2036; Lilly filed a non-CVD obesity extension in Jul 2036, under review. Novo's gambling-disorder phase 3 reported topline in Nov 2036 meeting its primary endpoint; filing planned 2037, so no compulsion indication. Other triple agonists remain in phase 3 in China and the US with no US filing. Implants remain phase 1–2. No oral matches tirzepatide. Net prices, which drifted down 3–5% a year through 2034, were flat in 2035–36.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation on full-dose regimens and the leading cause of conditional-track checkpoint failure. Pediatric 6–11 semaglutide GI discontinuation ~9% in STEP Young. Compounded retatrutide titration errors add GI ED visits.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; absolute cases up with volume; no change in per-user risk.
Still no causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. Litigation centres on exocrine insufficiency.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; EPI MDL first bellwether (Mar 2035) returned a $38M plaintiff verdict on failure-to-warn for pre-2031 use, under appeal; no new science.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR holds at ~1.3 after 2+ years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles in users 65+. Normal-weight users lose a similar share as lean mass. No new signal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning (Jul 2028) retained; DXA code; bimagrumab adjunct; resistance-training statements on retatrutide and amycretin labels.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal in adults, AUD populations, or the STEP Young pediatric cohort.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Unchanged estimates: clinically meaningful anhedonia ~7–8% of users vs ~3% of controls, ~10–11% on retatrutide. Low-dose exposure (~18M licensed calm, Reset and longevity users plus gray microdosers) is still unmeasured; the NIH normal-weight cohort has enrolled baseline only. No new study changed the status.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling. The 2034 FTC–FDA consent orders still bind four platforms only; no new orders.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months; fastest after retatrutide 12 mg and after gray supply interruptions. Conditional-coverage checkpoint failures created a new, predictable stop point.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; underpins chronic-therapy framing and adherence-conditioned coverage.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron, vitamin D in low-intake users; low ferritin in adolescent girls; gray and compounded users rarely get the annual panel.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language (2031); same language on the 6–11 semaglutide label.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× EPI incidence after 5+ years continuous semaglutide (~4 vs ~2 per 1,000 person-years); partial recovery in about half who stop 12+ months. Tirzepatide excess still small and non-significant.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class labelling (Mar 2031); tirzepatide under continued review.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling; effects in people without obesity
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of semaglutide follow-up; ~22M current users have BMI under 30. Children aged 6–11 now start weekly semaglutide with no final-height data for any incretin. No new signal confirmed.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone and growth PMRs continue and were extended to the 6–11 semaglutide approval; NIH normal-weight cohort enrolling.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved or compounded product passed ~61,000 by mid-2036. Compounded retatrutide units-vs-mg dosing errors drive a steady stream of poison-centre calls (~8× 2025). No repeat of the 2033 insulin-pen cluster; isolated counterfeit hypoglycaemia cases continue. Rerouted vials tested at 0–310% of label, ~19% endotoxin-positive.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts unchanged; India's B2C registration in force since Jan 2035; the 2034 state felony laws stand; federal personal-importation enforcement still weak.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The 48-month liraglutide PMR update (2035) shows the ~0.7 cm/year height-velocity deficit in prepubertal starters persisting with no catch-up, consistent with prior data. STEP Young showed a similar-direction deficit over 68 weeks. Swedish ARFID HR unchanged at ~1.8. Final adult height unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Growth-monitoring language on both under-12 labels; specialist initiation recommended, not required; no federal age restriction; eleven state bans and the EMA specialist restriction stand.

food_and_beverage.state: About 53% of households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~15–17% from 2025, sugary drinks ~14%. Dollar sales flat on price and protein lines. After the 6–11 approval, lunchbox snack makers report softer volumes in suburban non-ban states such as Georgia and North Carolina and steady volumes in ban states, the first time state law shows up in kids' snack data. Longevity aisle keeps growing.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes down ~20% from 2025, beer ~13%. AUD fills (~1.5M) and calm plans keep eroding heavy drinking. Further brewery consolidation; Midwest bar closures continue at a slower pace. Non-alcoholic still under 6% of volume.

restaurants.state: Traffic roughly flat, checks smaller; portion tiers universal. Some chains print 'on-plan' menus as a default rather than a special. QSR value menus still carry low-density zips and regain-driven late-night traffic after checkpoint failures and seizures.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking; childrenswear brands add 'slim-regular' runs. Resale, stretch and size-flex subscriptions serve cyclers. Structured athletic wear grows.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing because conditional-track designs reward lean-mass scans. Gyms sell checkpoint-prep packages timed to six-month employer weigh-ins. Longevity clinics bundle labs and in-person microdose visits in the seven in-person-rule states.

insurance.state: Employer weight coverage rose to 37% but is mostly conditional 'earned coverage'. Pharmacy trend ~+7% with no price relief. PBMs sell checkpoint verification as a service. Part D premiums rose for 2035 and 2036. Insurers report the checkpoint drop-off (~22%) as savings.

pharma.state: Volume up ~27% on flat net prices. Lilly cannot fill 12 mg retatrutide demand and watches compounders sell copies under the shortage listing. Novo held semaglutide exclusivity in court and took the 6–11 label. Amgen's MariTide gains from clinic-administered conditional tracks. Litigation and counterfeit-defence spending above $1.3B a year.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on is no longer a signal; being off is. Intake forms at dentists and gyms ask 'Current incretin? If no, reason', and 'none' prompts a follow-up. The tiers still read through the body: scanned and muscled means covered and coached; monthly clinic bruise means employer track; lean-before-the-drug with a daily pill means longevity; regained means a failed checkpoint, a seizure or a bad batch.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: In Charlotte and Austin the status object is still the biomarker printout, and a nine-year-old's growth-and-HbA1c chart now sits beside it in Mecklenburg County pediatric portals. In Memphis, where Tennessee's ban bars under-12 weight prescribing, some parents drive to Southaven, Mississippi clinics, which is legal; Medicaid families mostly do not. Along the Columbus corridor, checkpoint weigh-ins set the calendar for shift leads.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are short and protein-led by default. Hosts ask guests 'are you on?' the way they once asked about allergies, and plan portions accordingly. Bread Alone claims ~900 congregations. Birthday cake slices at school parties in non-ban suburbs are now sized for children who will not finish them.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list status like a diet once was: 'on (oral)', 'on (monthly)', 'between courses', 'off by choice'. 'Off by choice' reads as either principled or a warning. Couples schedule around shot days, checkpoint months and calm-plan doses.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: In the upper tier, appetite and craving are noise a subscription manages, and admitting to strong hunger is mildly embarrassing, like admitting to smoking. In lower-income communities appetite still signals lost access, and in ban states parents of under-12s defend children's appetites as normal. Unmuted is smaller and older; its argument that being off is a choice is now the minority position.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Weight-dose anhedonia ~7–8% vs ~3% controls, ~10–11% on retatrutide; low-dose rate still unmeasured among ~5.2M calm/focus, ~2.1M Reset and ~11M longevity licensed users plus several million gray microdosers. Quiet, a telehealth platform founded after the 2034 consent orders and not bound by them, reports ~1.8M subscribers (inside the calm and Reset totals) and sells reduced craving and emotional quiet as the product. ~13M workers in conditional or monitored tracks; ~24% of large employers reimburse calm/Reset fees.
interior_life.framing: Feature. Quiet and its imitators advertise 'turn the volume down' and 'freedom from wanting' on podcasts and streaming in the 44 states without social-media ad bans. Gray peptide storefronts sell 'calm stacks' outright. The four bound platforms still say 'metabolic balance'. Clinicians still call it a dose-related side effect; employers say 'steadiness'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Conditional coverage made adherence a payroll fact: missing a checkpoint can cost a worker the coverage and, under the 30% guidance, raise their premium. At Columbus 3PLs and national call centres, monitored-track enrollees still reach shift lead about twice as often. The Ohio ADA suit survived a motion to dismiss in 2035; trial set for 2037. Recruiters for remote customer-service roles ask about 'regulation practices', and candidates mention Quiet unprompted.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Sportsbook handle per active account down ~20% from 2032 in high-density states; operators run 'not for the quiet' campaigns aimed at off-drug men under 35. Slow television and ambient games are a mainstream category. 'Off' memoirs now sell as contrarian; Unmuted off nights continue in Cleveland and Birmingham to smaller rooms. Comedians mock the audience for not laughing, and it does not laugh.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Desire mismatch remains the leading couples-therapy complaint. Quiet's marketing shows couples 'who stopped fighting', and therapists see couples who stopped fighting and stopped everything else. Partners on Reset plans for pornography report less conflict and less sex, and do not always call that a problem.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: No new state action: the restriction coalition stalled after 2034, and 2035 sessions produced nothing on telehealth, children or premiums. In the 2036 campaign several candidates mention being on a drug in passing and nobody follows up; being off is what reporters ask about. Gaming lobbies push FTC complaints against Quiet without result. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence.

state.regulatory_posture: Permissive and inert. The FDA approved weekly semaglutide for ages 6–11 and converted tirzepatide's dementia label, and listed retatrutide 12 mg in shortage in Apr 2035, which reopened compounding. No new statutes, rules or consent orders at state or federal level; the eleven-state under-12 bans, seven in-person rules and six ad bans stand unchanged. Congress passed nothing.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: None new. TrumpRx operates at frozen manufacturer prices. The Medicare Bridge pilot was not revived. The 2027 tri-agency 30% guidance now underpins most new employer coverage, which is conditional by design.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in law, deeper in practice. Earned-coverage designs feed PBM fill data, clinic administration records, connected-scale weigh-ins and HbA1c results into checkpoint decisions. Brokers sell checkpoint-pass-rate analytics. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE unchanged; Army recruit oral pilot continues. DOT 2033 guidance stands: prescribed, disclosed incretins are non-disqualifying, so compounded use is disclosable and imported vials are not.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India's B2C export registration took effect Jan 2035 and rerouted rather than stopped flow, via UAE free zones, Mexico and the Dominican Republic. Chinese reta, ami and cagri vials move through research-peptide fronts. The US cash-to-Indian-generic gap widened slightly to ~45–65× as US prices stopped falling.

events.event: Novo Nordisk files weekly Wegovy for children aged 6 to 11 on STEP Young data, seeking a label beside generic liraglutide in the 39 states without under-12 bans

Philadelphia jury awards $38 million in the first exocrine-pancreas bellwether against Novo; weeks later Novo, Lilly and Amgen keep 2035 cash prices unchanged and a Delaware court upholds Novo's semaglutide formulation patents against generic filers

FDA adds retatrutide 12 mg to its drug shortage list as demand outruns Lilly's fill lines; compounding pharmacies and telehealth sites begin selling copies for $129–199, alongside rerouted Chinese 'reta' and 'ami' vials

UnitedHealthcare and Cigna roll out 'earned coverage' for employers: six months of weight-drug coverage, then continued only with verified adherence and weight or HbA1c targets; employer coverage reaches 37% by November
FDA approves Wegovy for obesity in children 6 to 11 with growth-monitoring language; prescriptions begin in non-ban states, and some Memphis parents drive to Mississippi clinics

Telehealth start-up Quiet, not party to the 2034 consent orders, passes 1.8 million subscribers with ads promising 'freedom from wanting'; a Pew survey finds 61% of adults say not taking an incretin 'usually has a reason worth asking about'

open_tensions: Conditional coverage expanded access and built a cliff: ~22% of earned-coverage enrollees failed a checkpoint, lost coverage and faced higher premiums under the 30% guidance, and about half moved to compounded or gray product, which stays outside the Ohio lawsuit's scope.

The retatrutide shortage listing legalised compounded copies at half Lilly's price. When Lilly's new fill capacity ends the shortage, ~4.2M compounded users will be pushed toward a $299 product that is not getting cheaper or toward unregulated vials.

Weekly semaglutide is now approved for 6–11-year-olds in 39 states and banned by statute in 11, with a persistent height-velocity deficit and no final adult height data; legality now depends on where a child lives and whether the family can drive across a state line.
Blunting is now sold openly by platforms outside the 2034 consent orders, while the low-dose anhedonia rate among ~18M licensed users is still unmeasured and no regulator has acted.

prose.headline: The Question Now Is Why You're Not: 98 million Americans are on it, prices are frozen, and the coverage comes with a weigh-in
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 a little over one American adult in three takes an incretin drug, close to ninety-eight million people, and almost half have tried one. Nobody finds this interesting anymore. What gets attention is the person who isn't on one. Dentists' intake forms ask for a reason. Dating profiles list 'off by choice' the way they once listed 'vegan'. In a Pew survey this spring, three in five adults said a person not taking one usually had a reason worth asking about.

Prices fell steadily for years and then stopped. In March 2035 a Philadelphia jury returned the first pancreas verdict against Novo, and a Delaware court kept generic semaglutide off the market. After that neither Novo, Lilly nor Amgen cut a single price. The Wegovy pill still starts at $149 on TrumpRx, MariTide is still $219, and Lilly's 12 mg retatrutide, the dose that comes closest to surgery, is still $299. Lilly cannot make enough of it. When the FDA put it on the shortage list, compounding pharmacies were legally allowed to sell copies, and telehealth sites now sell them for $129 to $199. The import trade grew at the same time. India's parcel rules sent shipments through Dubai and Mexico instead of stopping them, and Chinese research-peptide vials now include amycretin and cagrilintide copies as well as 'reta'. More than twenty-two million Americans use something outside the licensed system.

Employers did start paying, with conditions attached. Employer coverage rose from 29 to 37 percent in two years, and nearly all of the increase is what UnitedHealthcare and Cigna call earned coverage. The plan pays for six months. After that it keeps paying only if the pharmacy and the connected scale show the worker took every dose and lost enough weight. About one enrollee in five misses a checkpoint. They lose coverage, often pay a higher premium under the 2027 rule that still allows it, and roughly half of them buy vials. Insurers book the drop-off as savings, and gyms sell checkpoint-prep packages.

Children are now part of the market. In December 2035 the FDA approved weekly Wegovy for children aged six to eleven. The label requires growth monitoring, because children who start early still grow about seven millimetres a year more slowly and nobody yet knows their adult height. In thirty-nine states pediatricians now prescribe it, and in Charlotte a nine-year-old's HbA1c sits in the family portal next to a parent's DXA scan. In the eleven states that banned under-twelve prescribing in 2034, the bans stand, because no legislature anywhere acted on incretins in 2035 or 2036. Some Memphis parents drive to clinics in Southaven, Mississippi. Families on Medicaid mostly do not make the trip.

The quiet is being sold as a product. The 2034 consent orders bind four platforms, and newer ones are not covered. Quiet, the largest of them, has 1.8 million subscribers and advertises on podcasts with the line 'freedom from wanting'. Its ads show couples who have stopped fighting. Couples' therapists see couples who stopped fighting and stopped most other things too. The rate of flattening at low doses has still not been measured. Sportsbooks run ads aimed at young men who are off the drug. Slow television is a mainstream category. Freight hubs outside Columbus still promote monitored-track workers to shift lead at twice the usual rate, and the lawsuit over that practice goes to trial next year.

In the 2036 campaign some candidates mention their own prescriptions in passing and nobody asks a follow-up question. Spirits volumes are down a fifth from 2025 and snack volumes by about a sixth. Lunchbox snack makers can now see the state bans in their sales data. Nothing has broken.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Dana Kowalczyk sets two alarms on the first Tuesday of the month. The first one is for work and the second one is for the scale.

She steps on it barefoot at 5:10. The display says 171.4 and then SYNCED. Checkpoint is in nineteen days. She needs 168.

At the Groveport cross-dock she clocks in, and Marisol from the clinic trailer waves her over for the monthly shot. Her plan pays all of it but forty dollars, as long as nothing in the app turns red. Marisol swabs the belly and the bruise from last month is already yellow. 'You're tracking,' she says, reading the tablet.

At lunch a new loader, Trey, eats a whole sub. Somebody asks him, friendly, whether he's between courses. He says he isn't on anything. The table goes quiet while everyone waits for him to explain.

After shift she picks up Eli, who is ten and wants to know if he can get the shot like Jaden in Kentucky. 'Not in Ohio, bud.' He says Jaden's mom drives him across the bridge. Dana says Jaden's mom has a different car.

At home Rob is in the garage with the vial he gets from a guy in Reynoldsburg. His coverage dropped in March when he missed 5 percent by a pound and a half. He draws it into an insulin syringe and squints at the lines.

After dinner, which is chicken and half of everything else, they sit on the couch. Rob says the evening is nice. Dana agrees. Neither of them can remember what they used to talk about.

least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism/magnitude: The rollout starts in July 2035, yet employer coverage supposedly jumps from 29% to 37%, with ~31 of those points in newly designed earned-coverage plans, in about four months. Employers redesigning plans, enrolling workers and being surveyed in that window is asserted, not shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: weeks later Novo, Lilly and Amgen keep 2035 cash prices unchanged and a Delaware court upholds Novo's semaglutide formulation patents against generic filers
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: A verdict against Novo and a Novo-only patent ruling are offered as the cause of a three-company freeze. Lilly and Amgen face neither the verdict nor that ruling, and the retatrutide and MariTide price holds have no shown chain from either.

least_plausible_claims.quote: ~22M users have BMI under 30, ~7.5M under 25. Adult obesity ~30.9%.
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: 97.7M current users minus 22M leaves ~75M users with BMI ≥30. Add the ~16% of adults (~44M) who have obesity and never used, and obesity would be ~43%, not 30.9%. The obesity figure does not reconcile with the user and BMI counts.

rationale.badness: Measured against 2026, the world is clearly worse. 35.4% of adults are on drug, and ~22M use gray or compounded product with ~61,000 adverse-event reports. Coverage is mostly conditional 'earned coverage': a ~22% checkpoint failure rate costs workers coverage and raises premiums, and half of those fail-outs move to gray product. Quiet openly markets 'freedom from wanting' while low-dose anhedonia stays unmeasured and no regulator acts (reward-blunting note, framing). Children 6–11 are on a weekly drug with a persistent growth deficit and no adult-height data, and access to it depends on state of residence and family income. Employer adherence surveillance, being off-drug read as suspect, and flattened couples are structural and normalised, though there is no mass death or collapse.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is traceable: adoption +7.4pp, stalled prices, conditional coverage, the Wegovy 6–11 filing and approval, no new safety signal, no new class, a retatrutide shortage-driven gray resurgence, Pew normalisation, no new state action, and Quiet as the marketed feature. mechanism: The pediatric path and the shortage listing reopening compounding are well chained. The attribution of the three-company price freeze to one Novo verdict and a Novo patent ruling is thin, and the 29→37% employer coverage jump in about four months is asserted (claims 1 and 2). magnitude: Adult on-drug (35.4), ever-used (45), income thirds, the age check, payer mix (sums to 97.7M), Medicare spend ($41.9B) and pediatric counts all reconcile and sit inside the envelope, and the pediatric approval lands exactly 12 months after filing. least_plausible_claims.quote: but ~31 of those 37 points are 'earned coverage' designs

least_plausible_claims.quote: Causes: EPI bellwether verdict and litigation reserves, a 2035 district ruling upholding Novo's semaglutide formulation patents against Paragraph IV filers
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a $38M verdict against one company, which is trivial next to $1.3B a year in defence spending, is offered as a reason for Novo, Lilly and Amgen all to freeze cash prices at once. Lilly and Amgen were not defendants. The patent ruling concerns exclusivity that already ran to about 2031, so it explains nothing about cash prices.

Magnitude: 6–11 use was about 0.12% in 2034, and weekly Wegovy was approved only in Dec 2035. Tripling to 0.4% (about 70–100k new children) within roughly six months, in the 39 non-ban states, is an implausibly fast uptake for a new pediatric label with specialist-initiation guidance.

rationale.badness: Measured against 2026 (11% on drug, voluntary access, anhedonia a niche complaint), this world carries every 2034 harm and adds more. Coverage depends on weigh-ins: about 22% fail a checkpoint, lose coverage and face higher premiums, and about half move to gray vials. About 18M people use imported or research-peptide product and 4.2M use compounded product, with unmeasured contamination risk. Children aged 6–11 are medicated in a patchwork by state line with a persisting height-velocity deficit. Quiet sells 'freedom from wanting' while the low-dose anhedonia rate stays unmeasured and no regulator acts. Being off the drug now needs an explanation, which is structural, normalised pressure.

Anhedonia is sold openly as 'freedom from wanting' while the low-dose rate stays unmeasured and no regulator acts, so the harm is structural and normalised ('being off is what reporters ask about'). Mass death is absent, so the score stops short of 9.

least_plausible_claims.quote: ~22M users have BMI under 30, ~7.5M under 25. Adult obesity ~30.9%.

Children 6–11 are on a weekly drug with a persistent growth deficit and no adult-height data, and access to it depends on state of residence and family income. Employer adherence surveillance, being off-drug read as suspect, and flattened couples are structural and normalised, though there is no mass death or collapse.
